name: Trinidad and Tobago

legalStatuses.label: Registered business name
legalStatuses.plain: You run the business as an individual under your own name or a business name. You and the business are the same person for tax. Usually the simplest way to start.
needs: business address in Trinidad and Tobago
legalStatuses.feeNote: Sources differ: name reservation about TT$20 to TT$25 and registration about TT$200 to TT$220. Confirm the current fees with the Companies Registry.

legalStatuses.label: Limited company
legalStatuses.plain: The company is its own legal person, separate from you. It costs more to set up and has more paperwork, but it can limit your personal risk.
needs: registered office in Trinidad and Tobago
legalStatuses.feeNote: Incorporation costs more than a business name. One source gives about TT$2,200 in all. Confirm the current fees with the Companies Registry.

launchSteps.label: Search and reserve your business or company name
launchSteps.plain: Two businesses cannot have the same or a similar name. You can search and reserve online through TTBizLink (you need a TTConnect account).

launchSteps.label: Register the business name, or incorporate the company, with the Companies Registry
launchSteps.plain: Online through TTBizLink or at the Registry office. A company also needs a registered office in Trinidad and Tobago.

launchSteps.label: Register with the Inland Revenue Division (BIR file number)
launchSteps.plain: This is how you file income tax. Self-employed people also pay their tax in advance, each quarter.

launchSteps.label: Register with the National Insurance Board (NIBTT)
launchSteps.plain: Self-employed people must register and contribute. It gives you access to a pension and other benefits.

launchSteps.label: Register for the Green Fund Levy
launchSteps.plain: A company pays 0.3% of its gross sales into a national environment fund, every quarter.

launchSteps.label: Open a separate bank account for the business
launchSteps.plain: Keeping business money apart from household money makes your numbers clearer and your taxes easier to pay.

launchSteps.label: Register as an employer and prepare monthly payments
launchSteps.plain: With employees you pay deductions (income tax, NIS, Health Surcharge) each month. Confirm the deadlines with the IRD and NIBTT.

launchSteps.label: Register for VAT
launchSteps.plain: Required when your sales reach TT$500,000 in twelve months, or when you expect them to. Registration is free.

incomeTax.label: Income tax
incomeTax.allowanceNote: personal allowance per year (to confirm for 2026)
incomeTax.bracketText: 25% on chargeable income up to TT$1,000,000, then 30%

salesLevies.label: Green Fund Levy (0.3% of gross sales)

contributions.label: NIS
contributions.plain: National Insurance. It gives access to a pension and other benefits. Contributions are set by earnings class, so this is an estimate.

contributions.label: Health Surcharge
contributions.plain: A small fixed weekly amount for public health care (about TT$8.25 a week at most earnings levels).

vat.label: Value Added Tax
vat.registerNote: You must also register if you expect to reach it in the next twelve months. Registration is free.
vat.filingNote: Confirm your filing period with the IRD.

calendar.quarterlyTextPersonal: Pay your advance income tax instalment and your NIS contribution.
calendar.quarterlyTextCorporate: Pay your corporation tax instalment, and your Green Fund Levy (0.3% of gross sales).
calendar.annualTextPersonal: File your income tax return for the year before.
calendar.payrollText: Every month: pay payroll deductions for the previous month (income tax, NIS, Health Surcharge). Confirm the exact deadlines with the IRD and NIBTT.
calendar.vatText: If registered for VAT: file your VAT return for each period. Confirm your period with the IRD.

notes: Business levy: businesses with gross sales above TT$360,000 pay 0.6% of gross sales if that is more than their income tax. It is not payable in the first three years of a business, and it is not included in your estimate.
